route: Wrote an independent full-spectrum (np.fft.fftn, Parseval-exact) band-split relative L2 and compared it with operators.metrics.Frequency_Split_Relative_L2 on (a) synthetic fields, (b) the same error placed along x and along z, and (c) 23 pairs of real perovskite angle-stratum charge densities from /Pool/VASP_DATA/_derived/perovskite_grid at cutoff 64/8 = 8, the block's Lattice_Frequency_Cutoff. In (c) the neighboring run stands in for a copy-floor prediction.
value_found: (a) With the band set to the whole field (cutoff 1e9), the code returns 0.024577; Relative_L2 and the full-FFT version both return 0.031908. (b) A cos(3x) error of identical size (Relative_L2 0.022475 either way) gives low band 0.023647 along x and 0.016721 along z; the full-FFT version gives 0.023612 for both. (c) Over 23 real perovskite pairs, the code's low-band value differs from the Parseval-exact value by between -2.4% and -16.6% (median -10.0%). The high band differs by -2.3% to +1.9%.
evidence: The code takes norms over the rfftn half spectrum without weighting: 'difference = np.linalg.norm((prediction_modes - truth_modes)[mask])'. Interior last-axis modes therefore count once, not twice, so the kz=0 and Nyquist planes are over-weighted relative to every other mode. The result depends on the error's direction and does not reproduce Relative_L2 on the whole band. The DeepONet report rows 0.016584 / 0.122894 (report.md lines 353-354) come from this function, called at deep_operator_network/report.py:1451. The bias on real perovskite pairs reaches 16.6%, in the claim's 11-16% range. I did not recompute the exact floor predictions the claim used.

route: Rebuilt the arm population independently from the strain assignment map (All_Strain_Arms, Interior_Levels, Strain_Tensor_By_Run_Path; no checkpoint, no report Main). Counted the interior (scored) levels whose runs carry different six-component strain tensors. Then loaded those levels' charge densities from the derived store (Loaded_Strain_Charge_Density, 40^3) and scored an ideal predictor against the code's truth: the representative run's (runs_by_level[level][0]) own field, averaged over the two functionals the way Manifold_Member_Arm_Predictions does, compared by the repo's Relative_L2 to the all-runs level mean that Cached_Level_Field uses as truth.
value_found: 423 scored levels; on 66 of them (one_angle_shear 38, two_angle_shear 28) the runs sharing a level carry 3 different tensors (shear in the xy / xz / yz plane or plane pair, same magnitude), because Strain_Level drops the plane label. A perfect member given the representative (xy) tensor scores median relative L2 0.02297 on those 66 (mean 0.02369, range 0.00226-0.04871). That is 25.2x the pooled bracketing floor (0.000911) and 9.4x the member's pooled median (0.002452). The member trains on per-run fields with each run's own tensor (ManifoldBlock). Both floors are fit and scored on the plane-averaged fields: the bracketing floor interpolates averaged corners to the averaged truth, and the radial-basis floor maps the representative tensor to the averaged field for both training and evaluation, so neither is penalized. Whether the kill stands without the 66 levels cannot be reached: results.json stores only summary rows, not per-level member errors, and recomputing them needs the checkpoint loader, which the rules forbid.

route: The perovskite_folds split file and the stored perovskite_grid charge densities (64^3, fractional positions are cubic perovskite 0/0.5). For each holdout test run I tried all 48 lattice-vector sign flips and axis permutations. Each operation predicts a partner factor tuple: flipping a vector maps an angle to 180 minus the angle, so factor 0.8 maps to 1.2 and 0.9 to 1.1. I transformed the test field the same way and computed relative L2 against the partner in the non-holdout pool. The 52-run training subset is the pool minus every fifth sorted key, mirroring Perovskite_Train_Validation_Split. As controls I also scored the untransformed fields.

route: Recomputed the fold-zero reduced-salted floor per run from the store and the split file by calling the floor building blocks (LoadedBlock for the split, Element_Vocabulary, Fitted_Salted_Floor, Evaluation_Points, Predicted_Correction, Trilinear_Interpolate) in my own script, not the report; added per-run diagnostics (mean and spread of the predicted correction, mean of the true correction density - superposition, mean density, elements absent from the shell vocabulary) and summarized per unit myself.
value_found: Unit median 0.111713 and interquartile 11.583332 reproduced exactly (21 units, 42 runs). The 9 held-out-chemistry units (each carrying one element absent from training: Fr, Ba, Al, Tl, Cu, Rh, Sc, Bi, I) score 11.41-12.01 normalized MAE; the 12 others 0.093-0.113. In every held-out run the predicted correction has mean 8.400-8.406 e/A^3 with spread only 0.11-0.15 (a near-uniform offset), while the true correction's mean is within +-0.011 and the mean density is 0.70-0.74 (offset about 12 times the mean density); in-vocabulary runs' correction mean is -0.011..0.008. Mechanism in code: Species_Shell_Features drops atoms whose element is not in the training vocabulary, and the ridge (no centering, intercept plus near-constant broad-shell columns) then returns a large constant. The interquartile is the gap between the two groups, not a spread of ridge corrections. The 95% interval [2.832035, 7.337816] was not recomputed (bootstrap not run), but with 9 of 21 units near 11.7 and 12 near 0.1 it follows from the same split.
